title: XR & Spatial Computing
summary: Virtual reality, augmented reality, spatial computing, and the next generation of human-computer interaction.
bodyHtml:
🔁 XR is still early. Meta has spent $50B+ on Reality Labs with losses. Apple Vision Pro is generation one. The killer app has not shipped: but the hardware is converging. This is a 2027–2030 inflection, not a 2025 event.

Why This Sector Matters

Spatial computing replaces the flat screen with an immersive overlay on physical reality. Every interface: work, social, gaming, navigation: gets redesigned for a 3D layer. The smartphone market took 10 years from iPhone launch to ubiquity; AR glasses will be faster because the enabling AI, display, and chip infrastructure already exists. The hardware timeline is: 600g VR headset (current) → 100g mixed reality → 30g AR glasses (2030–2032). At 30g and $300, this is a mass-market consumer product. The investment case today is in the infrastructure that will power that transition: GPU compute, spatial AI, and the content platforms that will have millions of users before the glasses arrive.

Sub-Themes

Meta Quest 3 (at $499) has made Meta the overwhelmingly dominant VR platform: over 60% market share in standalone VR. The hardware investment ($15B+ per year in Reality Labs) is a bet that the platform that wins VR wins the next computing paradigm. Meta's strategy is to sell hardware at near cost, profit from the social and app platform on top. This is identical to how Amazon subsidised Kindle hardware to sell books. The flywheel: cheap headsets → developer ecosystem → more content → more users → more data for AI → better experiences → more users.

The loss is real ($4–5B per year in Reality Labs), but Meta's core advertising business generates $50B+ per year. The R&D bill is affordable. When the glasses hit consumer form factor and price point, Meta will have the most trained AI, the largest developer ecosystem, and the most user data in the spatial layer.

META
Leader: META · 92% no rivals identified

At $3,499, Apple Vision Pro is not a consumer product: it is a developer and enterprise preview. Apple is building the ecosystem and proving the design language before scaling the supply chain for a mass-market version (rumoured 2026–2027 at $1,500). The Vision Pro's optics (micro-OLED, 4K per eye), eye tracking, and spatial audio are the best in the industry. VisionOS is the first new Apple operating system in a decade. Apple's historical pattern: iPod → iPhone → iPad: suggests the mass market version follows 3–4 years after the pioneer product. The iPod of VisionOS is coming.

AAPL
Leader: AAPL · 90% no rivals identified

Roblox has 88M+ daily active users building and monetising within its platform: predominantly Gen Z and younger. It is already a user-generated metaverse without the headset requirement. When glasses arrive, Roblox does not need to build the content: it already has millions of creators and billions of hours of engagement. The equity case is: user-generated platform (zero content cost) + virtual economy ($4B+ in developer payouts) + AI tools that accelerate creator productivity. Roblox is the latent XR content platform most investors haven't repositioned into yet.

RBLX
Leader: RBLX · 70%

Snap's core social product is struggling, but its AR developer platform has 300,000+ AR developers who have built 3M+ AR lenses. Snapchat Lens Studio is training the next generation of AR content creators on Snap's platform: creators who will need an OS when glasses ship. Snap Spectacles (AR glasses, 5th generation) are the most advanced consumer AR glasses currently shipping, though at niche volumes. Snap is simultaneously the most undervalued and most risky pure-play AR name: the developer ecosystem has real value; the core social business is under structural pressure from TikTok and Instagram.

Causal Signals

  • Hardware price and weight are the adoption gating factors. When standalone AR glasses hit 100g and $500, the addressable market jumps from millions to billions. Track Meta, Apple, and Qualcomm's annual hardware spec announcements.
  • Developer ecosystem growth: Roblox creator count, Meta Horizon developer MAUs, and Apple Vision Pro app approvals are the leading indicators of content depth that drives consumer adoption. Content follows hardware; adoption follows content.
  • Enterprise XR adoption: Boeing, Airbus, and automotive OEMs are deploying AR-guided manufacturing. Enterprise contract announcements from PTC, Siemens, and Microsoft HoloLens are the near-term revenue signal that proves industrial use cases before consumer scale.
  • AI spatial rendering: NVIDIA's DLSS and Omniverse, Apple's spatial AI, and Meta's AI-generated environments reduce the compute cost of immersive graphics. Each generation of GPU makes XR more accessible; track annual GPU architecture releases.
